models_evaluated: UNet-derived auto-contouring model (femoral heads, bladder, rectum; 0.35T MRI)

links.outcome: Expert-consensus vs clinically used contour agreement (DSC) and dose differences before vs after auto-contouring
links.effect: Contouring behavior changed after automation. Femoral head DSC vs expert consensus rose from 0.91 to 0.93 and rectum fell from 0.88 to 0.85. Max-dose differences were not statistically significant.
links.quote: Automation bias was observed, but it had little deleterious effect on treatment planning.

links.outcome: Presence of automation bias and its dosimetric consequence in planners using AI contours
links.effect: Automation bias was observed in planners. Only 4 deviating slices in 2 patients were graded low clinical significance, none moderate or high. Dose differences were not significant.
links.quote: Automation bias was observed, but it had little deleterious effect on treatment planning.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the real-world clinical implementation and human factors (specifically human review/editing and automation bias) of deep learning auto-contouring in MRI-guided radiotherapy.

primary.practice: clinician review and editing of automated contours
